correctness.rationale: The quotient-lifting argument correctly uses independent equitable blocks and positive uniform interblock degree. A hypothetical chordless quotient C_l (l=4 or l>=6) induces a graph T with minimum degree at least 2 and a homomorphism T->C_l. Its shortest cycle is chordless; l=4 makes T bipartite so this is a forbidden even induced cycle >=4, and l>=6 makes T triangle- and pentagon-free, so its shortest cycle is forbidden length 4 or >=6. Removing internally adjacent automorphism orbits preserves equitability, hence the class. Orbit-constant barycentric coordinates give a simplexwise affine PL homeomorphism of geometric fixed points with Ind(Q_H). Woodroofe supplies vertex decomposability, nonpure shellability and torsion-free wedges. Scope includes all finite H, but not arbitrary nonequitable quotients.

originality.rationale: Woodroofe proves vertex decomposability for the forbidden-cycle graph class, and the orbit-barycenter identification is a standard combinatorial fixed-point method. The new substantive structural closure is that equitable independent-block quotient retains precisely the same induced-cycle restriction; this lets Woodroofe apply simultaneously to all subgroup geometric fixed spaces, beyond chordal/forest cases.
